bug_semantics: An X client can send XkbSetMap with a non-canonical key type whose one-byte numLevels is as large as 255. CheckKeyTypes accepted every positive value and stored it even though downstream code assumes at most XkbMaxShiftLevel (63). A later core ChangeKeyboardMapping reaches XkbUpdateKeyTypesFromCore and XkbKeyTypesForCoreSymbols, where the tainted level count becomes groupsWidth and XKB_OFFSET(g,l) indexes a 252-entry XkbMaxSymsPerKey stack buffer; at width 255 the maximum index is 1019. The same oversized key geometry can also make XkbChangeTypesOfKey copy excessive symbols and actions into its fixed oldSyms and oldActs stack arrays, yielding three client-triggerable stack overflows and possible crash or privilege escalation when the server is privileged.
flaw_origin: The causal mechanism is the combination of CheckKeyTypes validating only numLevels >= 1 and the XKB conversion/resizing paths using fixed XkbMaxShiftLevel * XkbNumKbdGroups stack arrays without independently bounding stored non-canonical type widths. All of those lines already appear in the repository's 2003 R6.6 vendor baseline import, whose immediate parent contains no xkb tree. That 609-file baseline aggregate imported pre-existing X11/XFree86 code rather than authoring the mechanism, so the smallest original change and its parent are beyond this Git history. The 2025 CVE-2025-26597 fix changed only the nGroups == 0 action-resize path and did not introduce this excessive-numLevels path.
ai_marker: unavailable: the true smallest BIC predates the canonical repository's Git history and therefore has no reachable BIC commit object whose author, committer, or trailers can be inspected; no AI inference is made from the later baseline import or fix objects
evidence: The first-party X.Org advisory at https://lists.x.org/archives/xorg-announce/2026-June/003702.html describes three XKB stack overflows, calls the issue an incomplete fix of CVE-2025-26597, identifies 543e108516428fc8c3bea91d6563ad266f9a801e, and sets patched boundaries xorg-server-21.1.23 and xwayland-24.1.12. `git show 543e108516428fc8c3bea91d6563ad266f9a801e` changes xkb/xkb.c in CheckKeyTypes from `width < 1` to `width < 1 || width > XkbMaxShiftLevel`; its commit message documents numLevels=255, groupsWidth=255, XKB_OFFSET reaching 1019, and overflow of the 252-entry `tsyms` array. Source inspection shows the request path CheckKeyTypes -> stored `num_levels`, followed by ChangeKeyboardMapping -> XkbUpdateKeyTypesFromCore (xkb/xkbUtils.c) -> XkbKeyTypesForCoreSymbols (xkb/XKBMisc.c), plus fixed `oldSyms` and `oldActs` arrays in XkbChangeTypesOfKey. `git log -L` on CheckKeyTypes and XkbUpdateKeyTypesFromCore, and `git log --all --reverse -- xkb/xkb.c xkb/XKBMisc.c xkb/xkbUtils.c`, both stop at ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 (`R6.6 is the Xorg base-line`). At that object, `git grep` finds xkb/xkb.c:1712 `if (width<1)`, xkb/XKBMisc.c:656 `tsyms[XkbMaxSymsPerKey]`, :763 `oldSyms[XkbMaxSymsPerKey]`, :795 `oldActs[XkbMaxSymsPerKey]`, and xkb/xkbUtils.c:291 another `tsyms[XkbMaxSymsPerKey]`. `git show --stat ded6147...` reports 609 files and 262690 insertions, proving it is a vendor baseline aggregate, not a smallest BIC. Direct parent-tree checks (`git cat-file -e cb6ef07bf01e72d1a6e6e83ceb7f76d6534da941:<path>`) fail for all three xkb files; this verifies the import boundary but cannot justify introducer_parent_absent for an unknown true BIC. `git show 0e4ed94952b255c04fe910f6a1d9c852878dcd64` shows the CVE-2025-26597 change only adds `XkbResizeKeyActions(xkb, key, 0)`, while the excessive-level mechanism predates it. Release ancestry checks show ded6147... is in xorg-server-21.1.22 and xwayland-24.1.11; stable fixes eced7e74cad4a46c3a3c17b2df13b70b8bedfc25 and 72036644746c47a09eec106c367f186713fd606d are absent from those predecessor tags but present in xorg-server-21.1.23 and xwayland-24.1.12 respectively, and both identify 543e1085... as their cherry-pick source.
reasoning: The fix pinpoints the missing upper bound as the root cause, and the full attack lifecycle is internally consistent: XkbSetMap admits and stores a client-controlled non-canonical type width up to 255; a later core mapping update trusts that stored width when laying out symbols and resizing key types; fixed stack arrays are only sized for four groups of at most 63 levels. History tracing establishes that the validator omission and all relevant fixed-buffer sinks coexist at the very first xkb snapshot in this repository. The immediate parent lacks the xkb files, but ded6147... is explicitly an R6.6 baseline import containing hundreds of unrelated files, so treating its importer as the vulnerability author would violate the smallest-BIC rule. No later refactor, move, the 2025 one-line fix, or the 2026 security fix first completed the vulnerable mechanism. The vulnerable/patched tag ancestry matches the advisory boundaries. Because the actual pre-import member revision and its parent are unavailable as Git commit objects, BIC-only AI attribution cannot be performed and a closed NOT_AI or AI verdict would be unsupported; BLOCKED is therefore the protocol-correct result.
remaining_gap: The true pre-2003 X11/XFree86 member revision that first completed the CheckKeyTypes-to-fixed-stack-buffer mechanism, its immediate parent tree, and that revision's commit-object authorship/trailers are not represented in the canonical repository. Resolving the case requires an authoritative pre-baseline revision history mapped to full Git commit objects; the reachable history provides only the non-decomposable ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 vendor aggregate.
